articles.headline: Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more
articles.description: Tuesday's news that the Premier League found Man City guilty of 100-plus charges of breaking financial rules is a landmark moment. But what comes next: what punishments are on the table, and how does the appeals process work?
articles.body:
Manchester City's guilty verdict on 114 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules is a landmark moment in global sport.

City continues to assert their innocence and have signaled their intention to appeal before Friday's deadline. But the Independent Commission's verdict could hardly have been more damning, accusing the club of "sham" contracts involving its Abu Dhabi owners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" that contributed to inflating revenues and reducing costs by over £900 million. Witnesses in City's defense were accused of dishonesty, and the club was found to have "clearly intended to circumvent" Premier League rules.

The breaches relate specifically to a nine-year period (2009-18), but the shockwaves permeate far beyond. Pep Guardiola's trophy-laden legacy is in doubt. The Premier League's reputation and viability is in the balance. Rivals may seek retribution through compensation claims, triggering challenges that could last for years.

Meanwhile, City's punishment is yet to be determined. Under Section W, Rule 54 of the Premier League's Handbook, they are facing a punishment ranging from a reprimand to expulsion. There could be a fine, a points deduction and a transfer ban.

City's aggressive protestations of innocence only contribute to the widespread uncertainty and reduces the likelihood of all parties coming together to reach agreement on a settlement for the time being. Beyond that, the legal complexities are vast.

ESPN has spoken with one of the United Kingdom's leading law firms, Howard Kennedy, in pursuit of clarity. Partners Kyle Phillips and Lois Langton head the firm's sports group, with Phillips specializing in business crime and regulatory process. On Thursday, the pair talked with ESPN's James Olley to answer some basic questions and follow-ups about what this all means and what's next.

Editor's note: This interview has been edited for clarity and length.

How would you characterize the commission's findings?

Kyle Phillips: I think it's worse than many people expected. The words that were used by the commission in the findings report, caveated with the fact it's very difficult to read because a lot of it is redacted and there's no evidence or appendices that they keep referring to, but the language that they use is very strong.

"Sham" is one point. You've got the disguised payments, sorry -- the "disguised funding scheme," overstating commercial revenue, the amounts involved ... it is all quite shocking. And it is quite a strong statement to say that you find the witness evidence that was given to be "dishonest" -- a powerful word in any decision.

In any regulatory proceedings, it takes a lot for them to use that word.

How deliberate is this language? Are they effectively trying to preempt or dissuade an appeal?

Phillips: Although the panel's names are redacted, you'd expect them to be experienced lawyers. They would be quite cautious about their language and very deliberate in what they say. So yo

articles.headline: Spurs' Victor Wembanyama not interested in promoting betting sites
articles.description: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama said Thursday that he isn't interested in promoting sports betting sites.
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- Count Spurs star Victor Wembanyama as one of the professional athletes who isn't interested in promoting sports betting sites.

The Frenchman expressed his view on the subject Thursday after a training camp workout.

"Absolutely not," Wembanyama said when asked if he'd ever consider promoting a sports betting website. "I will never do that. Honestly, I think it's very sad to see some players promote it. Everybody does whatever they want, but without me."

Wembanyama was subsequently asked how he makes decisions about which brands to promote.

"In the past, there was a dimension of money," he said. "Not anymore. Even if I said that, I've refused plenty, much, much more money than I've made for things that were not [in line with] my values. And now, I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence with who I can share messages and values. Obviously, we earn millions and millions. This is not our biggest strength. Our biggest strength is inspiring. I want to inspire in a good way. That's the strongest thing I can do."

Several of Wembanyama's NBA peers currently promote sportsbooks and prediction platforms, including LeBron James, who moved from DraftKings to Polymarket in September, Kevin Durant (FanDuel), who is also an investor in Kalshi and Giannis Antetokounmpo, who became a shareholder at Kalshi back in February.

"The internet is full of opinions," Antetokounmpo wrote in a since-deleted post on X, announcing the move. "I decided it was time to make some of my own. Today, I'm joining Kalshi as a shareholder."

Three-time MVP Nikola Jokic, in 2023, became the first brand ambassador of Superbet in Serbia.

The NBA's collective bargaining agreement treats sports betting operators and prediction markets the same when it comes down to player partnerships. Players aren't allowed to promote betting on any market related to the NBA. But they are allowed to endorse and hold de minimis equity investments in sports betting companies with some restrictions.

Wembanyama, meanwhile, enters his fourth season in the league coming off San Antonio's first appearance in the NBA Finals since 2014. The two-time All-Star last season became the first player to unanimously win NBA Defensive Player of the Year after leading the league in blocks for the third-consecutive season.

Wembanyama, 22, finished third last season in voting for NBA MVP.

articles.headline: Jacoby Brissett and Jameis Winston meet as starting QBs as the Cardinals visit the Giants
articles.description: — Jacoby Brissett and Jameis Winston go way back to their college days more than a decade ago.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- — Jacoby Brissett and Jameis Winston go way back to their college days more than a decade ago. 


              Brissett's best friend, Nick O'Leary, played tight end at Florida State with Winston, and the two have stayed in touch over the years.


              “Somebody like that I always root for — besides this weekend — and have a ton of respect for him,” Brissett said.


              Not long ago, they were journeyman backup quarterbacks closer to the end of their respective NFL careers than the beginning. On Sunday, they’ll meet as starters when Brissett and the Arizona Cardinals visit Winston and the New York Giants. 


              Brissett has been No. 1 on the depth chart since training camp opened, while Winston assumed his spot after Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury in Week 2. It has been a mixed bag for each of them, and the difference in their next matchup may come down to who does not turn the ball over.


              Winston expressed pride in avoiding that mistake while beating Tennessee to get the Giants to 2-1. They have yet to score a touchdown in the seven-plus quarters since he stepped in for Dart.


              “Everyone’s so used to me throwing for 500 yards and throwing interceptions,” Winston said. “If we were having a conversation about me throwing interceptions and throwing for 300 yards, y’all wouldn’t be asking me a question. But when God allows me to manage a football game, now it’s, ‘Does he still have it?’”


              The questions are there in large part because New York made a move Monday to add another QB, acquiring J.J. McCarthy in a trade with Minnesota. Coach John Harbaugh said Winston is the starter for now.


              Brissett appears ensconced in that role for the 1-2 Cardinals, backed up by Gardner Minshew and with rookie Carson Beck waiting in the wings. The 33-year-old through three games has completed 70.1% of his passes for 652 yards, four TDs and one interception.


              “You’ve got to change the picture on him,” Giants edge rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux said. “You’ve got to get him to hold the ball. I think we’ve got to run, we’ve got to play fast, we’ve got to hit and we’ve got to defend MetLife.”

articles.headline: Battle of the Bays features winless Buccaneers and struggling Packers
articles.description: — The Battle of the Bays features two struggling teams searching for an identity and a win.
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- — The Battle of the Bays features two struggling teams searching for an identity and a win.


              The Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-3) need a victory even more than the Green Bay Packers (1-2) on Sunday. They're trying to avoid an 0-4 start because only one team in NFL history — the 1992 Chargers — overcame that to make the playoffs.


              But 1/3 isn't much better so there's plenty of urgency for the Packers, who were booed at Lambeau Field following an embarrassing loss to Atlanta in their home opener last Thursday.


              At least Green Bay has quarterback Jordan Love. Tampa Bay is turning to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels after Baker Mayfield dislocated his right thumb in a loss to Minnesota.


              “For us, it’s just trying to get a win," Bucs coach Todd Bowles said. "(Jalon Daniels) is not playing by himself. Everybody has to do their job. We’ve got to coach it the right way on both sides of the ball, including special teams. He’s got to play and just do his job. We’ve got 21 other guys that (are) going to be out there playing with him, so he’s not by himself. It’s (a) nervous (feeling) but it’s exciting at the same time because you get to see somebody play. No matter where you come from, your first NFL game has to come at some point, whether you’re a first-round pick or whether you’re a free agent. You’ve got to touch the field for the first time at some point, and then you’ve got to play. He’s just got to play.”


              While the Buccaneers have a new quarterback, Love will have new faces blocking for him. The Packers have had to revamp their offensive line because of several injuries. They signed veteran guards Kevin Zeitler, Laken Tomlinson and Mekhi Becton this week.


              “It’s just a matter getting to work, seeing how fast those guys can pick up the offense,” Love said of the recent additions. “I think at the end of the day, putting the best five out there and there’s always going to be some competition in those positions, so do whatever the team feels best at that position.”


              Need to know
              Green Bay (1-2) at Tampa Bay (0-3).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox.


              Latest odds: Packers by 1 1/2.


              Against the spread: Packers 0-3; Buccaneers 0-3.


              Last week: Packers lost to the Falcons 35-14; Buccaneers lost to the Vikings 23-16.


              Last meeting: Buccaneers beat the Packers 34-20 on Dec. 17, 2023, in Green Bay.


              Series record: Packers lead 34-24-1


              Matchup to watch
              Packers wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden vs. Buccaneers cornerbacks Zyon McCollum, Jacob Parrish and Benjamin Morrison. McCollum has allowed a passer rating of just 69.3 in the first three games. He’ll be tested by Watson, who has 17 catches for 284 yards and four TDs.


              Stats and stuff
              — Packers Q

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Dolphins move towards split backfield to replace De'Von Achane
articles.description: Marcel Louis-Jacques has the latest update on how the Dolphins backfield will operate after Achane's injury.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 1: Dolphins move towards split backfield to replace Achane

By Marcel Louis-Jacques

Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II was one of the most popular adds in fantasy this week. The former Doak Walker Award winner offers rare size for the position and handled a 20-touch workload in place of De'Von Achane in Week 3.

We all know opportunity is a premium commodity in fantasy, but it's important to remember that Gordon was the Dolphins' only other active running back last week. Jaylen Wright, the former fourth-round pick, has seldom seen the field during his three-year career but ran for 107 yards and a touchdown on 24 carries filling in for Achane against the Jets last season.

Wright offers sub-4.40 speed and a versatile skill set. Speaking to Wright and Gordon this week, they sound ready to share the workload moving forward.

Dolphins Coach Jeff Hafley envisions a split backfield, so expect them to ride with the hot hand. 

Sept. 30: TNF injury updates, 10 trends to know for Week 4

By Michael F. Florio

Rico Dowdle did not practice to start the week and is out for the Pittsburgh Steelers' "Thursday Night Football" matchup with the Cleveland Browns. With Dowdle sidelined last week, Jaylen Warren handled the bulk of the opportunities, playing 90% of the snaps and garnering 17 carries and four targets. Warren finished with 176 total yards and 20.6 fantasy points (RB8).

Warren has a chance to build off of that in Cleveland, as the Browns have allowed the sixth-most yards on outside runs and have missed tackles at the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. Warren should be started over David Montgomery, Quinshon Judkins, Omarion Hampton, Rhamondre Stevenson and Jadarian Price.

Trends to know for Week 4

Defenses have altered the way they play Drake Maye since last season's playoffs. Teams are rushing four men -- or fewer, at times -- at a high rate against the New England Patriots but have still been able to create quick pressure. Last week, the Jacksonville Jaguars rushed four or fewer on 82% of dropbacks and still created pressure in under 2.5 seconds, on average. Each team has played Cover 6 at least 15% of the time against Maye.

Simply put, teams are able to get to Maye quickly without blitzing, meaning they are able to drop more players into coverage. Maye has to make quick decisions, and it is not allowing enough time for his receivers to consistently get open. It also has seemingly sped the clock up in his head.

articles.headline: The Seahawks will be looking for a rebound on Sunday while the Chargers just want a win
articles.description: The Seattle Seahawks need just a few tweaks, according to coach Mike Macdonald. No need to overhaul the defending Super Bowl champions in the wake of one loss.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks need just a few tweaks, according to coach Mike Macdonald. No need to overhaul the defending Super Bowl champions in the wake of one loss. 


              The Seahawks fell 33-31 last weekend on the road against the Washington Commanders, snapping a 12-game winning streak. They'll look to rebound at home on Sunday when they face the winless Los Angeles Chargers. 


              “In our world, we try to remain as consistent as possible and think about the things that we can control within our process, that we can improve,” Macdonald said. "Obviously, the context after a loss is a little bit different than after a win, but we try to keep the mentality the same. It’s good exercise in practicing what we preach this week.”


              One of the areas that needs a look is the running game. The Seahawks gained just 44 yards on the ground against the Commanders and just 19 in the second half. 


              Rookie running back Jadarian Price lost a fumble early in the game and finished with 15 yards on five carries.


              Help may soon be on the way. Zach Charbonnet is still on the physically unable to perform list, but once he practices, there will be a 21-day window to return to the active roster. Macdonald said Charbonnet could return to practice Thursday. 


              Charbonnet, who was sidelined by a torn ACL, ran for 730 yards and 12 touchdowns last season. 


              “He’s doing a great job and he’s in a great position mentally. It’s just about what’s the best time and how does that create the most opportunities to get them ready to play?” Macdonald said. 


              But again, the Seahawks aren't looking for a wholesale run-game rebuild. 


              “Sometimes you just don’t get the run game off the ground in a certain game and you don’t hit the panic button, you just go back to work and try to find more solutions and just keep trying to solve problems and go try to make it better," Macdonald said. 


              As for the Chargers, well, they just need a win after starting 0-3. Only one team has ever gone to the playoffs after an 0-4 start. That team was the 1992 San Diego Chargers. 


              Following the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills last weekend, coach Jim Harbaugh said quarterback Justin Herbert needs to improve. 


              Herbert has thrown for 627 yards and three touchdowns with four interceptions through three games. 


              And he's been sacked eight times. 


              “Be better. Be better,” Harbaugh said. “And that drives Justin, that drives me, that drives his position coach, that drives Mike (McDaniel), the coordinator. I mean, it drives us all.”

articles.headline: Johnson and Glenn match wits once again as the Bears host the Jets in Week 4
articles.description: — Ben Johnson's time in Detroit — a formative experience that led to his current job as coach of the Chicago Bears — was shaped in part by going against Aaron Glenn's defense in practice with the Lions.
articles.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- — Ben Johnson's time in Detroit — a formative experience that led to his current job as coach of the Chicago Bears — was shaped in part by going against Aaron Glenn's defense in practice with the Lions.


              Johnson remembers it well.


              “He certainly lights a fire under you," he said. “I still remember to this day being next to him in training camp, and you can hear him. You can hear him. And when the defense makes a play, he lets you know."


              Johnson goes up against Glenn once again on Sunday when the Bears host the New York Jets. Glenn took over in New York in January 2025, right after Johnson was hired by Chicago.


              Johnson, 40, was the offensive coordinator for Detroit while Glenn, 54, was the defensive coordinator with the Lions. Glenn faced their former boss last weekend, losing to 31-24 to Dan Campbell's Lions in Detroit.


              Glenn recalled planning for practice with Johnson in one of their first meetings after he took over the offense.


              “Just having those conversations and seeing how he put things together, and then just talking offensive and defensive football was good to have,” Glenn said. "But the one thing, we were so competitive in move-the-ball situations on how we wanted to beat each other, but it made both of us better, I will say that. He’s a damn good coach.”


              Glenn and New York are preparing for a Chicago team with an uncertain situation at quarterback, at least publicly. Caleb Williams is rehabbing a right hamstring injury. Case Keenum passed for two touchdowns in Monday night's win over Philadelphia, but Johnson hasn't identified the starter for the matchup with the Jets.


              Chicago also could go with Tyson Bagent, who emerged from the NFL’s concussion protocol on Sunday.


              Whoever gets the call for the Bears will face an improved Jets defense, directed by Glenn, who was a defensive back in the NFL for 15 seasons.


              “You can see how he played the game as a player has translated to how he coaches, and his guys take that same identity as well,” Johnson said. "Like I said, a ton of respect for him and he’s a heck of a competitor.” 


              Need to know
              New York Jets (1-2) at Chicago (2-1).

              Latest odds: Bears by 3 1/2.


              Against the spread: Jets 2-1, Bears 2-1.

              Series record: Bears lead 9-4.

articles.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
articles.description: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
articles.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.
